findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 restriction and exposes a hidden website to anonymous viewers
findings.body: `website` is gated by `untrusted_attributes`, so for a TL0 user viewed by an anonymous or restricted scope it is omitted. The new `website_name` attribute is added to the plain `attributes` list (line 43), not to `untrusted_attributes`, and `include_website_name` only checks `website.present?` without calling `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)`. The result is that the website's domain (and now its path, via the new same-domain branch) is still serialized and rendered by user.hbs line 66 for restricted users. This defeats the intentional hiding of TL0 website data. Adding `:website_name` to the `untrusted_attributes` list (around line 105) would apply the existing gate, and the custom `include_` method would be unnecessary.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' and is never called
findings.body: The serializer's include hooks follow the `include_<attr>?` convention (see `include_email?`, `include_card_image_badge_id?`, `include_suspend_reason?`). This method is named `include_website_name` with no question mark, so ActiveModel Serializer will not find it when deciding whether to emit the attribute. The intended `website.present?` condition therefore never runs, and `website_name` is emitted as `null` for every user with no website. Renaming it to `include_website_name?` would fix the contract, though the leak above still needs the untrusted gating.

findings.title: Domain comparison is case-sensitive, so mixed-case website hosts lose the path
findings.body: `URI(...).host` preserves the case typed by the user, but `Discourse.current_hostname` is compared with `==` here and with `ends_with?` and `split` below. A website such as `http://Example.com/user` on an instance at `example.com` does not match the first branch, falls through to the parent-domain check, and returns just `Example.com` with the path dropped. Hostnames are case-insensitive, so the host should be downcased before comparing.

findings.title: Homepage URLs with a trailing slash render as 'example.com/'
findings.body: For a website like `https://example.com/`, `URI(...).path` returns `"/"`, so the first branch returns `"example.com/"`. This is a very common way to enter a homepage and produces an awkward trailing slash in the profile. The path should be ignored when it is empty or `"/"`.

findings.title: Untrusted attribute list was not updated for the new website_name attribute
findings.body: The TL0-anonymous spec asserts that `bio_raw bio_cooked bio_excerpt location website profile_background card_background` are not serialized, but it does not include `website_name`. Because `website_name` is ungated, this spec gives false confidence: it would still pass while the domain leaks for restricted users. Adding `website_name` here and setting a website on the TL0 fixture would catch the regression.

findings.title: Missing coverage for the www/forum sibling-subdomain branch and for a blank website
findings.body: The `website_name` examples cover the exact-match branch and the parent-domain branch, but not the middle branch in the serializer (same label count, same parent domain, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forums.example.com`). That branch has its own path-appending logic and is untested. There is also no example for a user with no website, which is where `website_name` should return nil and the attribute should be omitted (the `include_` logic that is currently broken).
